newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN WANT TITLE - AND A PEACEFUL SEASON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN WANT TITLE - AND A PEACEFUL SEASON.

text.p: German league championship favourites Bayern Munich want a peaceful season for a change, as well as another title, when the campaign starts this weekend.
After a season marred by controversy and scandals, Bayern, who entertain promoted Kaiserslautern in their opening Bundesliga game on Saturday, won a record 14th title last May.
Now they want a 15th crown -- and a place in the European Cup final.
Their main rivals should be Borussia Dortmund, who were aiming at a rare third consecutive title last season and had to be content with third place.
But they made up for a relatively disappointing campaign with a brilliant run in the European Cup which ended with a shock 3-1 win over Juventus in last May's final.
Bayer Leverkusen, who settled for second place after giving Bayern a hard time, also stand a chance as well as VfB Stuttgart, who came fourth and won the German Cup.

"Our goals are the title and a place in the final of the European Cup," said Bayern coach Giovanni Trapattoni. "My favourites for the title are Bayern, Dortmund and Leverkusen," he added without taking too many risks. "Stuttgart will also be dangerous."

Juergen Klinsmann, who said he was tired of the atmosphere at the club, left Bayern for Sampdoria. He has been replaced by Brazilian striker Giovane Elber, who signed from Stuttgart for 12.5 million marks ($6.9 million).
Another signing was French international defender Bixente Lizarazu, who joined from Athletic Bilbao and is likely to take up a new role as a midfielder.
Dortmund, meanwhile, made few changes but hired a new coach in Italian Nevio Scala after Ottmar Hitzfeld became the club's sports director.
"There are three or four strong teams capable of winning the title and we're one of them," said Scala, on opera lover who has a German wife and speaks fluent German.

Scala, who joined from Perugia but is remembered for having led Parma to victory in the 1993 European Cup Winners' Cup and 1995 UEFA Cup, faces his first test away to newly-promoted Hertha Berlin on Sunday.
Hertha, one of three clubs to move up to the first division with Kaiserslautern and Wolfsburg, will be one of the attractions of the new season.

The club from Berlin, who dominated German soccer in the 1930s, will field a team made up mostly of new players. Their most spectatular reinforcement was Dutch international striker Bryan Roy, formerly with England's Nottingham Forest.
Leverkusen lost Paulo Sergio, now with Roma, and replaced him with another Brazilian midifielder, Emerson, who was with Gremio.
Last season's runners-up play their first match on Friday away to Schalke, the club from Gelsenkirchen who won the UEFA Cup.

After losing Elber, Stuttgart bought Nigerian striker Jonathan Akpoborie from Hansa Rostock. They will continue to rely on the playmaking skills of Bulgarian Krasimir Balakov and on the scoring instinct of German international Fredi Bobic.
"I believe Akpoborie is just as strong as Elber," said Stuttgart trainer Joachim Loew, whose team are at home to Munich 1860 on Friday.
